welcome_lead: Today you'll explore trends down the alkane series and a key test for alkenes.
meta_desc: GCSE Chemistry Organic Chemistry — trends in alkanes (boiling point, viscosity, flammability), structural formulas and the bromine water test.
final_note: You learned how alkane properties change with chain length and how to spot an alkene with bromine water.

walkthroughs.body_html:
As chain length goes up, properties change in a pattern.

Longer chains: boiling point ↑, viscosity ↑ (thicker), flammability ↓ (harder to ignite).

Short chains (methane, propane) are gases that ignite easily. Long chains (bitumen) are thick, sticky and hard to burn.

Each line is a bond. Carbon makes 4 bonds, hydrogen makes 1.

Ethane has two carbons joined by a single line, each carbon also joined to 3 H atoms. Ethene has two carbons joined by a double line (C=C), each carbon also joined to 2 H atoms.

Add a few drops of orange bromine water to the sample and shake.

With an alkene: bromine adds across the C=C bond and the orange colour decolourises (goes colourless).

With an alkane: no reaction, orange colour stays.

mcqs.q: As alkane chain length increases, boiling point…
options: decreases
stays the same
increases
doubles every time

mcqs.q: Bromine water with an alkene goes…
options: orange → colourless
colourless → orange
orange → blue
no change

mcqs.q: How do alkenes typically react with bromine?
options: Water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen gas when they boil.
By electrophilic addition — bromine adds across the double bond to form a dibromoalkane.
The alkene polymerises with bromine to form a long chain.
Bromine substitutes for a hydrogen on the alkene, releasing HBr.

mcqs.q: Why does atomic radius increase down a group?
options: Atoms get bigger down a group because they have more protons attracting more matter.
Atoms get bigger down a group because nuclei swell when they have more neutrons.
Each successive element has an additional electron shell, increasing the distance of outer electrons from the nucleus.
Water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen gas when they boil.

mcqs.q: When water boils, what is broken?
options: The covalent bonds between hydrogen and oxygen atoms are broken when water boils.
The alkene polymerises with bromine to form a long chain.
Water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen gas when they boil.
Intermolecular forces (hydrogen bonds) between water molecules are broken — the O-H covalent bonds stay intact.
